newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rexrodt says 1996 growth in line with expectations.
newsitem.headline: Rexrodt says 1996 growth in line with expectations.

text.p: Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt said on Thursday Germany's 1.4 percent economic growth last year was in line with the government's projection of a 1.5 percent expansion.
He said conditions were positive for a further improvement of the economic climate and stronger growth in 1997.

"The world economic environment is developing positively, and the conditions for investment have improved," he said. Government budget consolidation will continue and employment will increase, he said.
The government plans to release its economic projections for 1997 at the end of January.
Exports and capital investment were the main driving factors behind 1996 growth, but growth remains too weak to sustain itself or to have a positive effect on the labour market, he said.

"This makes it clear how urgent it is to continue basic reforms to strengthen economic forces. Wage negotiators and policy makers must support structural changes for more employment and to further improve conditions in Germany."
